inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-06-30: 1,470,194,681 issued less 106,399,200 treasury = 1,363.8m outstanding, plus 10.9m dilutive potential shares (H1 FY2026 interim, diluted EPS note) = 1,374.7m. 64.2m unvested awards excluded by the company as anti-dilutive. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The planned cancellation of 79.3m treasury shares on a US dual listing does not change the outstanding count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Pro forma: reported net debt US$1,069.0m at 2026-06-30 (financial debt 1,739.8 ex deferred financing costs, cash 670.8) + US$140.0m dividend paid 2026-07-15 (post balance date, price is ex) + US$178.5m BEIS 85% acquisition consideration (closed Oct 2026, funded from cash and RCF). Cash shown is the residual 670.8-140-178.5. Lease liabilities (US$473.5m at FY2025) EXCLUDED - leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). Minority put options excluded; NCI charged as leakage in the cash tax driver.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Company 'adjusted free cash flow' FY2025 = OCF 506.3 - capex 93.8 - lease principal 166.2. Lease interest (37.5) is already inside OCF. The CSV FreeCashFlow (412.5) excludes lease principal and is NOT the owner basis.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net debt company; finance income (FY2025 9.4) not stripped.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, adjusted EBITDA reconciliation 'Share-based compensation expense' 9.2 (FY2024 13.5); no net-share-settlement tax outflow disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of treasury shares 42.9 (FY2024 157.6, H1 FY2026 50.0). A repurchaser: the flat count is funded, and buybacks exceed the small SBC charge.
inputs.fx_note: USD->HKD 7.8479 (Yahoo HKD=X regularMarketPrice, 2026-10-16). HKD pegged 7.75-7.85; rate inside the band. No US listing yet for a parity check (the planned US ADS dual listing is not complete). All flows modelled in USD and converted at this rate to HKD per share.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows (HKD pegged), so a USD-built rate: risk-free 4.2% (UST 10y), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.35 for a geared consumer-discretionary/travel cyclical -> cost of equity ~11.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (term loans SOFR-based, EUR 4.375% 2033 notes) -> ~4.1% after tax. Market weights: equity ~US$2.3bn, net debt ~US$1.4bn (37%). WACC ~8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. Same rate in all scenarios; cyclicality is charged in the bear flows and weight, not by a scenario-specific WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) leases as operating cost. The EBITDA driver is the company's Adjusted EBITDA, which already deducts ROU amortisation (FY2025 170.5) and lease interest (37.5) - an accounting lease charge of 208.0 vs cash 203.7 (principal 166.2 + interest 37.5). lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0 and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. D&A excludes ROU amortisation (depreciation 65.5 + non-lease amortisation 20.4 = 85.9), so tax EBIT is not charged the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI (FY2025 share of profit 23.5 of 312.5, ~7.5%; dividends to NCI 21.7) charged once as leakage inside cash_tax_rate_path: 1-(1-0.26 tax)(1-0.06 NCI share of NOPAT) ~ 30%. No NCI deduction in the bridge. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT (606.8-9.2-86.0)=511.6 x 0.70 = 358; less after-tax net debt interest ~54 = 304 vs attributable NI 289 + ~16 after-tax of excluded impairment/other expense = 305.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations (USD flows / HKD quote, IFRS 16 leases, NCI). Samsonite is an asset-light global luggage and bags brand owner - an operating company, so owner FCF is the right stream. FY0 is FY2026E (H1 actual 1,680.6 + H2 at H2 FY2025 +1%) because the balance sheet is mid-2026: year 1 is FY2027, and the H2 FY2026E levered owner FCF that will land against the June net debt is added in the equity bridge, so no half-year is counted twice or dropped. FY2026E adjusted EBITDA ~US$561m (15.9%, 15.4% ex the US$16.6m IEEPA tariff refund). BEIS (85%, ~US$210m 2025 sales) is held at cost in the bridge and its revenue excluded from the growth paths. House and street nearly coincide (SBC ~0.3% of revenue) but the band is not degenerate, so band_position is reported.

equity_bridge.note: Acquired Oct 2026 for US$178.5m cash; consideration is in net_debt, so the asset is carried at cost (value-neutral). Revenue excluded from the growth paths.

H2 FY2025 adjusted FCF was 234.8 (246.3 FY - 11.5 H1). H2 FY2026E taken at ~195 after lower EBITDA and higher marketing, less ~5 SBC and ~10 NCI dividends. Cash that reduces the June net debt before year 1 (FY2027) starts.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle organic growth (pre-COVID run-rate ~3-5%, FY2018-FY2025 revenue CAGR -1.2%, IATA 2026 traffic +4.9%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (15.8% 3y, 20.3% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue (6.7% 3y) and EPS (-1.6% 3y). All 5-year rates start from the FY2020 COVID trough (US$1.28bn loss, equity rebuilt from 634m), so neither equity nor 5y revenue CAGR is a usable forward rate. Revenue is below FY2018 seven years on.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (CSV FCF - lease principal - SBC): FY2019 315.7, FY2020 -362.6, FY2021 192.8, FY2022 69.8, FY2023 269.7, FY2024 297.5, FY2025 237.1. The 50% 3y owner-FCF CAGR is a FY2022 working-capital-rebuild trough base. SBC is small (0.3-0.4% of revenue) and falling, so owner and reported growth diverge only through lease principal, which rose from 131m (FY2022) to 166m (FY2025) - faster than revenue as DTC stores grew.

base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (post-lease, pre-SBC) was 19.3% FY2023, 19.0% FY2024, 17.3% FY2025, ~15.4% FY2026E ex tariff refund. Base recovers to 17.5% - FY2025 level, not the FY2023-24 post-revenge-travel peak - as marketing at ~6.5% of sales is held and DTC mix offsets American Tourister price pressure.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: FY2023 3.0%, FY2024 3.1%, FY2025 2.7%; 3.0% mid-cycle with DTC store and BEIS investment. D&A 2.6% (FY2025 85.9 ex ROU = 2.5%).
base.wc_capture_pct_rationale: Wholesale-heavy (59%) distributor with inventory + receivables > payables; growth consumes ~15% of incremental revenue. FY2025 WC outflow 53.6 on falling sales was inventory build.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_rationale: ~26% unlevered cash tax (FY2025 cash tax 120.7 vs effective 25.2%) plus ~6% NCI leakage of NOPAT = 30%.

scenario_narratives.base: Travel demand normalises after the Middle East conflict shock and North American consumer softness of 2026: organic sales grow 3-4% (in line with IATA/UN Tourism traffic growth of 3-5%), lifestyle bags and DTC e-commerce keep gaining share, and American Tourister stabilises against VIP/Safari at the value end. Adjusted EBITDA margin rebuilds from ~15.4% (FY2026E ex refund) to 17.5% - the FY2025 level, not the 19% FY2023-24 peak - as marketing is held at ~6.5% of sales and tariffs remain a managed cost. Gross margin near 59-60% holds on scale sourcing. Net debt falls slowly while dividends and opportunistic buybacks continue.
scenario_narratives.bull: Lifestyle bags (now 37% of sales), TUMI's expansion beyond North America, DTC/e-commerce mix and BEIS's younger, female, digital-first franchise re-accelerate organic growth to 5-6%; operating leverage on the higher marketing base and DTC mix lift adjusted EBITDA margin back to the 19% achieved in FY2023-24. A completed US dual listing broadens the shareholder base (not modelled as value, but it is the catalyst for the market to price it).
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2025-26 margin slide is structural, not cyclical: value-tier share loss to regional discounters (VIP, Safari) spreads, wholesale partners keep destocking, tariffs and freight re-inflate, and the step-up in marketing fails to buy growth. Sales slip in FY2027 and grow only ~2% after; adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 14.5-15%. With ~US$1.4bn net debt against ~US$500-530m adjusted EBITDA, leverage stays ~2.7x - inside the 4.5x covenant, so this is a value case, not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: adjusted EBITDA has fallen two years running (FY2025, H1 FY2026), the business is a discretionary-travel cyclical with real leverage, and the value tier is losing share. Base 50%: guidance (stable Q3 constant-currency sales, sequential margin improvement) points to stabilisation, not recovery. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs growth re-acceleration AND a margin return to peak, two independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Samsonite is an asset-light brand owner whose value is a stream of lease-adjusted free cash flow; the market is pricing it at roughly 10% levered owner-FCF yield and ~6x post-lease adjusted EBITDA, i.e. as if the FY2025-26 margin decline persists. The DCF values flows on the company's own post-lease adjusted EBITDA (IFRS 16 rent kept as an operating cost, lease debt excluded), with NCI charged as leakage and SBC expensed. The terminal value is capped at 14x unlevered owner FCF (~7.5x terminal adjusted EBITDA) because this is a cyclical, not a compounder.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: each 1pp of terminal adjusted EBITDA margin is worth roughly HK$1.4-1.5/share; the base assumes recovery to FY2025's 17.3%, not FY2023-24's 19%.
Leverage amplifies equity value swings: pro forma net debt ~US$1.39bn is ~60% of market cap.
Travel/geopolitical shock (Middle East conflict already hit H1 FY2026) and US tariff policy reversals.
BEIS carried at cost - integration failure would make that a write-down; success is upside not in the numbers.
Terminal value is cap-bound (14x); the Gordon value at 8.5%/2.5% would be ~17x.
